Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:59: The fifth distinction concerning the matter of honor: the prophet said (Isaiah 43:7), "everyone that is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory," and so on. And they said in the Midrash (Yalkut Yeshayahu, remez 252), on this verse, in these words: is it possible for a person to be called by the name of the Omnipresent? Rather, the Omnipresent is called "merciful," as it is said (Psalms 103:8), "the LORD is merciful and gracious" - you too, be merciful and grant gifts freely. The Omnipresent is called "righteous," as it is said (ibid. 145:17), "the LORD is righteous in all His ways" - you too, be righteous. He is called "pious" [chasid], as it is said, "and pious [chasid] in all His works" - you too, be pious. Therefore it says, "everyone that is called by My name"; and it says (Joel 3:5), "whoever calls upon the name of the LORD shall be delivered"; and it says (Proverbs 16:4), "the LORD has made everything for His own purpose" - to this point. And in this manner that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained "everyone that is called by My name," it is understood that "whom I have created for My glory" means that this is the honor of the Holy One, blessed be He - that they do His will and His deeds in such a way that they are literally called by His name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:60: And the words of the Zohar (Terumah 155a) agree with this explanation; in these words: Rabbi Elazar opened and said (Ecclesiastes 9:8), "let your garments always be white, and let your head lack no oil" - this verse has already been established and stated [elsewhere], but come and see: the Holy One, blessed be He, created man in the secret of wisdom, and made him with great craftsmanship, and breathed into his face a soul of life, to know and to gaze into the secrets of wisdom, to know the glory of his Master - as it is said (Isaiah 43:7), "everyone that is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory - I have formed him, indeed I have made him." "And whom I have created for My glory" - precisely; and this secret we have learned, that the honor below - the secret of the holy Throne - is not established above except through the repair performed by the people of the world, when those people are righteous and pious and know how to make repairs. This is "and whom I have created for My glory" - for that Glory [kavod], to establish it with mighty pillars and to adorn it with the repair and adornment from below, because this "My glory" is raised through the honor of the righteous who are on earth - therefore "I have created him" in the image of the supernal Glory of these repairs within him - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:61: It follows that when the righteous man fixes his deeds in such a way that he is called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He - "merciful," "righteous," "pious" - the Shechinah, called "kavod," is established; and the righteous man was created only to repair the honor of the Shechinah, whose arousal depends on the repair of those below - as they explain in the Zohar (Bereshit 35a), on the verse (Genesis 2:6), "and a mist went up from the earth," and so on. And likewise in Parashat Terumah (155b), in explaining the verse (Psalms 119:126), "it is time to act for the LORD" - it says that at the time Israel strives in Torah, that "time," which is [the sefirah of] faith, is established in its repair and adorned in completeness as is fitting; but at a time when Israel neglects Torah, as it were, that "time" is not in its repair and is not found in completeness, nor in light - this is "it is time to act for the LORD," and so on - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:62: And this is the matter of "you have forgotten the Rock who bore you" (Deuteronomy 32:18), which is explained in the Zohar (Terumah, there), and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, also explained (Eichah Rabbah 1:33) that Israel adds strength to the supernal Gevurah, or weakens its strength, and so on. It follows that one who performs Torah and commandments gives honor to his Creator, for all creatures perform His honor and His will, and one who does not perform commandments diminishes the honor of his Creator.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:63: And so it says in Tanna Devei Eliyahu, brought in the Yalkut at the beginning of Ezekiel (remez 340), on the verse "son of man" (Ezekiel 2:1), in these words: son of fit men, son of righteous men, son of those who perform acts of loving-kindness, son of those who demean themselves for My honor and the honor of Israel. Another interpretation: "son of man" - to what may this be compared? To a king of flesh and blood against whom his wife and children rebelled - he arose and pushed them out of his house and sent them outside. Some days later he sent for and brought in one son from among her children. He said to him: son of so-and-so, come and I will show you my house and the house of My Shechinah that I have, apart from your mother - has My honor and My Shechinah been at all diminished, even though your mother stands outside? For this he appeared to Ezekiel, son of Buzi the priest, as it is said (Ezekiel 1:1), "and it came to pass in the thirtieth year," and so on - this was the first year; but in the second [vision] (ibid. 1:4), "and I looked, and behold, a stormy wind," and so on, "and out of the midst of it, the likeness of four living creatures" - after he showed him the whole Chariot, He said to him: son of so-and-so, this is My glory, and I have honored you above all the nations of the world - has My glory, or the house I built, been at all diminished? (Variant: or My Shechinah?) As it is said (ibid. 43:11), "and if they be ashamed," and so on. Perhaps you will say, I have no one to serve Me - but do I not already have nine hundred and six thousand myriads of ministering angels who stand before Me and sanctify My great Name every single day, continually, from sunrise to sunset, saying "holy, holy, holy," and from sunset to sunrise saying "blessed be the glory of the LORD from His place" - and needless to say the seventy nations that are on earth [also serve Me in their fashion]? So why do you do ugly things, and things that are unfitting, and kick against sufferings? But I will act for My Name's sake, that it not be profaned - to this point. And close to this text is brought at the end of the book Vayikra Rabbah (see 2:8), and from there I corrected the text and added a little to it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:64: The sixth distinction concerning the matter of honor is what the verse says (I Samuel 2:30), "for those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed" - and this matter of honor is explained in the Zohar and the Tikkunim in several distinctions. The first, concerning prayer, that one must direct his intention in it in the way of the secret - and this matter Rashbi explained (Vayelech 285a), and we will not copy his whole text since we must explain this primarily in the matter of prayer [elsewhere]; in these words: what is "and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed"? This is one who does not know how to unify the holy Name and bind the bond of faith and draw blessings to where they are needed, and to give honor to the Name of his Master - and whoever does not know how to give honor to the Name of his Master, better for him had he not been created. And along these lines of this distinction is what the verse says (Isaiah 29:13), "with his mouth and with his lips they honor Me, but their heart is far from Me" - and they explain that the honor of the supernal attributes comes through the illumination of the supernal soul, the soul of all souls, within them; and therefore, when a person's heart is attached in thought, he is attached to the inner dimension, and this causes the thought to spread within the attributes, and through them the Infinite and Keter spread, and everything becomes one unity - but if the heart is not there, these matters are found like a body without a soul, like broken vessels with no inner content.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:65: Further, there (Vayelech 285a), Rabbi Yehuda said, "and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed" - one who does not know how to give honor to the Name of his Master and does not concentrate on [saying] "amen," concerning which we have learned that greater is one who answers "amen" than one who recites the blessing - to the extent relevant here. And further on there: it is taught, whoever hears a blessing from the one reciting it and does not concentrate on "amen" for it, of him it is said "and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed," along the lines of (Malachi 1:6), "to you, O priests, who despise My name." And at the time it is required, what is his punishment? Just as he did not open blessings above, so they do not open [blessings] for him; and not only that, but when he departs this world, they proclaim before him and say: close the gates before so-and-so, let him not enter, and do not receive him - woe to him, woe to his soul - to this point. And they elaborate further there on the punishment of one who does not answer "amen."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:66: And the general practical conclusion drawn from this discourse - beyond the plain sense understood from his words, that one must concentrate on "amen," whether according to the plain meaning, or in the way of the secret, which is the more apparent, as it says "just as he did not open blessings," and so on - one must be careful not to speak during the repetition of the Shemoneh Esrei by the prayer leader, because they are blessings adjacent to one another, and if he speaks of his own affairs he will distract his mind and be unable to concentrate on "amen" even according to the plain sense; and likewise for every single blessing among the other blessings, he should not converse from the beginning of the blessing to its end, so that he may concentrate on "amen" properly. And besides this, he must be careful during the repetition of the Shemoneh Esrei by the prayer leader, for it is a great blemish [to speak then], as will be explained in the matter of prayer.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:67: Further, concerning the matter of "and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed," it is explained at the beginning of Parashat Va'etchanan (260b) that this refers to one who opens his eyes while praying; in these words: "and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed" - this refers to one who gazes at the Shechinah while he prays - and we copied the rest of this text in the Gate of Holiness, at the end of chapter 8.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:68: And in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah, Naso 8:3), on the verse "when a man or woman shall commit any of the sins of man" (Numbers 5:6), they comment on the verse "for those who honor Me I will honor"; in these words: another interpretation, "for those who honor Me I will honor" - refers to converts; they honor the Holy One, blessed be He, by abandoning their evil deeds and coming to take shelter under the wings of the Shechinah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, honors them. This teaches you that whoever straightens his ways honors the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Psalms 50:23), "whoever sacrifices thanksgiving honors Me"; and it says (Jeremiah 13:16), "give honor to the LORD your God before it grows dark," and so on. "And those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed" - these are the wicked, for since they turn away from the Omnipresent, the Holy One, blessed be He, esteems them lightly - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:69: Further, concerning the matter of the honor of the LORD - although the word "kavod" is not mentioned - is to rise to answer "amen, yehei shmei rabba," and so on, and "barechu"; and this is explained in the Yerushalmi: "arise, for this is the day which the LORD has delivered [Sisera] into your hand" (cf. Judges 4:14) - from here Rabbi Elazar said, when they answer "amen, yehei shmei rabba" and any matter of sanctity, one must stand on his feet - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:70: Further, concerning the matter of the honor of the LORD, is a warning to one who writes the [divine] Name, that he concentrate his intention on it properly. Rashbi, peace be upon him, was very strict about this in Parashat Acharei Mot (65b), in these words: he said to him, Elazar my son, from now on be careful not to write the holy Name except as is fitting - for whoever does not know how to write the holy Name as is fitting, and to bind the bond of faith, the bond of one with one, in order to unify the holy Name upon it, of him it is written (Numbers 15:31), "because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken His commandment, that soul shall utterly be cut off," and so on - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:71: Further, concerning the matter of the honor of the LORD, is what Rashbi explains (Vayigash 207b), that one who does not rise to occupy himself with Torah from midnight onward nullifies the honor of the LORD and is called "rebuked" - and we will copy his text further on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:72: Further, one must be careful not to speak mundane conversation in the synagogue - as they say in Parashat Terumah (131b), that whoever converses in the synagogue treats the supernal repair above with contempt - and we will copy the rest of this text in its place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:73: Further, the seventh distinction concerning the matter of honor is what the verse says (Psalms 50:23), "whoever sacrifices thanksgiving honors Me" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 43b): Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, one who sacrifices his [evil] inclination and confesses is as though he honored the Holy One, blessed be He, in both worlds, as it is said, "whoever sacrifices thanksgiving honors Me" - it does not say "yechabdeni" [will honor Me] but "yechabdaneni" [will doubly honor Me] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:74: Further, we find an eighth distinction of practical import, in what the prophet said (Isaiah 24:15), "therefore in the region of light, honor the LORD"; and likewise they said elsewhere (Judges 9:9), "and the olive tree said to them, should I leave my fatness, with which by me they honor God and man?" And although this is said as a parable, no word is written in the Prophets in vain - rather, certainly all of them pertain to practical matters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:75: And in the Midrash we find support for this matter, brought in the Yalkut, Parashat Beha'alotcha (remez 719): lamps of flesh and blood, whether of clay or of copper - all according to a person's honor; and the honor of Shabbat is its lamps, which are its honor. If you observe the lamps of Shabbat, I will show you the lamps of Zion, as it is said (Zephaniah 1:12), "and it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with lamps" - and I will not need you to see by the light of the sun, but rather I will illuminate you with My own glory, as it is said (Isaiah 60:19), "the sun shall no longer be your light by day, nor for brightness shall the moon give you light, but the LORD shall be your everlasting light" - and the nations are destined to walk by your light, as it is said (ibid. 60:3), "and nations shall walk by your light." And by what light does the Holy One, blessed be He, illuminate Israel? By the light of righteousness, as it is said (Malachi 3:20), "and the sun of righteousness shall rise for you who fear My name" - and all this, why? By the merit of the lamps that they kindle on Shabbat. Know how beloved the commandment of the lamps is before the Holy One, blessed be He - for even though the Holy One, blessed be He, has no need of light, He commands Moses to instruct Aaron (Numbers 8:2), "speak to Aaron and say to him, when you light the lamps" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:76: And at the end of his words there is also a practical implication for the lamps we kindle in the synagogue, which is comparable to the Temple - for it says, "know how beloved the commandment of the lamps is before the Holy One, blessed be He," that He commands Moses, and so on - and this applied to the Temple or to the Tabernacle.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:77: Further, concerning the virtue of the lamps, in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 31:4), in these words: another interpretation, "command the children of Israel" (Leviticus 24:2) - Bar Kappara opened, "for You will light my lamp" (Psalms 18:29): the Holy One, blessed be He, said to man, your lamp is in My hand and My lamp is in your hand. Your lamp is in My hand, as it is said (Proverbs 20:27), "the candle of the LORD is the soul of man"; My lamp is in your hand, to keep a light burning continually. But the Holy One, blessed be He, said, if you light My lamp, behold I will light your lamp - therefore, "command the children of Israel" - to this point. And therefore it is fitting to light lamps in the synagogue. And further, in the Midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:18), that Oved Edom was blessed for honoring the Ark, in that he would light one lamp in the morning and one lamp in the evening.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:78: Further, we find a ninth distinction concerning the matter of honor, and it is in the matter of charity. King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 14:31), "and he who honors Him is gracious to the needy" - the reason being that the poor and the needy are His "broken vessels," and the Shechinah dwells among them, as it is said (Isaiah 57:15), "I dwell in the high and holy place, and also with the crushed and lowly of spirit"; and therefore one who honors the poor with his wealth honors His Shechinah - and we will elaborate further on the matter of charity in the Gate specially devoted to it, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:79: Further, the tenth distinction, concerning the honor of father and mother, in the Yalkut, Parashat Va'etchanan (section 830), in these words: another interpretation, "remember the Sabbath day" [is placed next to] "honor your father and your mother" - and what does the one have to do with the other? Rather, to teach you that whoever honors his father and mother, no desecrations of Shabbat come by his hand, as it is said (Isaiah 56:2), "happy is the man," and so on - do not read "mechalelo" [who profanes it] but "machul lo" [it is forgiven him]. Let not a person say, since My Father in Heaven came before [my earthly father in obligation], I will perform the will of My Father in Heaven and set aside the honor of my father and mother - whoever seeks days, wealth, possessions, honor, and life in this world and the World to Come, and abundant life in the World to Come, let him perform the will of his Father in Heaven and honor his father and mother. Another interpretation, "honor your father" - Isaac fulfilled this, at the time he was laid before his father like a lamb led to slaughter. Another interpretation, "honor your father" - Joseph fulfilled this, as it is said (Genesis 37:12), "and Israel said to Joseph, are not your brothers pasturing [the flock] in Shechem?" [implying Joseph's willing obedience].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:80: Another interpretation: "honor your father" [is placed near] "you shall not murder" - what does the one have to do with the other? Rather, to teach you that if a person has the means and does not feed and support his father and mother, it is as though he were a murderer before the Omnipresent. Another interpretation: "honor your father" [and] "you shall not commit adultery" - to teach you that if a person has the means and does not honor his father and mother, it is as though he committed adultery before the Omnipresent. Another interpretation: "honor" [and] "you shall not steal" - if he does not perform the will of his father and mother, it is as though he kidnaps souls before the Omnipresent. Another interpretation: "honor" [and] "you shall not bear [false witness]" - whoever does not support his father and mother is as though he bore false testimony before the Omnipresent - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:81: And in the Yalkut, Parashat Vayigash (remez 152), on the verse (Genesis 46:1), "and Israel journeyed with all that he had," and so on, in these words: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, I went around to all the masters of aggadah in the south to tell me [the meaning of] this verse, and they did not tell me, until I came to Yehuda ben Padaya, the nephew of Bar Kappara, and he told me: when a teacher and a student are walking on the road, they first greet the student and afterward the teacher [with peace]. Rav Huna said: when Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi came to Tiberias, he asked Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish [about this]. Rabbi Yochanan said that a person is obligated in the honor of his father more than in the honor of his grandfather; and Reish Lakish said [that Jacob's journey with "all that he had"] was to offer sacrifice concerning the covenant of the tribes - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:82: Further, one must be careful concerning the honor of elders, as it is said (Isaiah 24:23), "and before His elders shall be glory." And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in the Sifrei (Beha'alotcha, piska 34): not in one place, nor in two places, but everywhere you find that the Holy One, blessed be He, gives honor to elders: at the Sanhedrin, "gather to Me seventy men of the elders of Israel" (Numbers 11:16); similarly (Exodus 3:16), "go and gather the elders of Israel"; and to Moses He said, "go up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadav and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel" (ibid. 24:1); "and it came to pass on the eighth day, that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel" (Leviticus 9:1). Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says: from where do we know that even in the future to come He will give honor to elders? As it is said, "and before His elders shall be glory" - it does not say "before His angels" or "before His prophets," but "before His elders." And so you find that the Holy One, blessed be He, grieves over one elder as much as over all of Israel, as it is said (Isaiah 47:6), "I was angry with My people, I profaned My heritage" - one might think this refers to all of them equally; the verse teaches, "upon the elder you have laid your yoke very heavily" [implying a special grievance for the elder]. And these matters follow a kal vachomer: if He who spoke and the world came into being is destined to give honor to elders, how much more so should flesh and blood give honor to elders - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:83: However, there is a dispute among the Tannaim (Kiddushin 32b): some hold that any elderliness [gray hair] is included, and some hold specifically elders learned in Torah. And in the Yalkut (Ki Tisa, remez 393), on the verse (Exodus 33:7), "and it came to pass that everyone who sought the LORD went out to the Tent of Meeting" - this teaches that whoever sees the face of an elder is as though he received the presence of the Shechinah - to this point. It appears that this is said of an elder learned in Torah, since Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was an elder learned in Torah. And likewise concerning this matter, brought in the Yalkut (see Yalkut Shmuel, section 96), on the verse (I Samuel 2:11), "and the boy Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli the priest" - it appears specifically an elder learned in Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:84: And in the Midrash (Ruth Rabbah 6:2), they say on the verse (Ruth 3:10), "blessed are you of the LORD, my daughter," in these words: Rabbi Yochanan said, a person should never refrain from going to an elder to have him bless him. Boaz was eighty years old and had not been remembered [with children]; once that righteous woman prayed for him, he was remembered. Ruth was forty years old and had not been remembered; once that righteous man blessed her, she was remembered - "blessed are you of the LORD, my daughter" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:85: And just as we are commanded to honor the Torah and its students, so we must be careful not to honor the wicked, as it is said (Numbers 24:11), "I said I would greatly honor you, but behold, the LORD has withheld you from honor" - and certainly Balak's words were not written in our Torah for nothing, but for practical implication; and further, the Name YHVH is mentioned among them, in saying, "the LORD has withheld you from honor." And the reason is: what we are commanded to honor the students of Torah and its elders for is because the light of the honor of the LORD flows within them, and one who honors them honors YHVH; but the wicked person, since he is removed from holiness, should not be honored - on the contrary, it is a commandment to hate him and demean him, in order to subdue the husk, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 139:21), "do I not hate those who hate You, O LORD," and so on. Therefore it is fitting to be careful not to greet a wicked person with peace; and so Rashbi explains (Va'era 23b) on the verse (I Samuel 25:6), "peace be to you, and peace be to your house" - they asked, did not David know that Nabal was wicked, and how could he greet him first with peace and call him "living"? And they answered that what David said, "peace to you," he said concerning the Holy One, blessed be He, as they explain there, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is the one called "living," and so on. And he said: from here we learn that it is forbidden to greet a wicked person with "peace" first; but if necessary, he should greet him as David did, blessing the Holy One, blessed be He, and it should appear that he says it for His sake. And should you say this was deception - no, for whoever elevates his intent to the Holy One, blessed be He, and it appears that he says it for His sake, is not deception; and whoever greets a righteous person with peace first, it is as though he greeted the Holy One, blessed be He, first - to this point. And what he said, "for whoever elevates his intent to the Holy One, blessed be He" - our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained similarly (Avodah Zarah 16b), on one who says, "the judge is reliable in my eyes [meaning God]" - and we will elaborate on the punishment of flatterers in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 12; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:86: Further, there is an eleventh distinction within the general category of honor: to be careful of anything that involves demeaning His honor, blessed be He, or shame - for the opposite of honor is disgrace and shame, as it says, "for those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:87: One must be careful concerning what the verse says in Parashat Shelach Lecha (Numbers 15:31), "because he has despised the word of the LORD," and so on, "that soul shall utterly be cut off," and so on - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained several ways [of transgressing] this, and in all of them one must be careful. They said in the passage "one who says the Torah is not from Heaven" (Sanhedrin 99a), in these words: our Rabbis taught, "because he has despised the word of the LORD" - this refers to one who says the Torah is not from Heaven; another interpretation, this refers to a heretic [apikoros]. "And has broken His commandment" - this refers to one who breaks the covenant of circumcision. "That soul shall utterly be cut off [hikkaret tikkaret]" - "cut off" in this world, "cut off" in the World to Come. From here Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i said: one who profanes sacred things, one who demeans the festivals, one who breaks the covenant of Abraham our father, one who shows favoritism in Torah not according to halachah, and one who shames his fellow's face in public - even though he has Torah and good deeds like Moses our teacher, peace be upon him - has no portion in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:88: It is taught elsewhere: "because he has despised the word of the LORD" - this refers to one who says the Torah is not from Heaven; and even one who says the whole Torah is from Heaven except for this one verse, which he claims Moses said on his own and not from the Holy One, blessed be He - this is "the word of the LORD he has despised." Even one who says the whole Torah is from Heaven except for this one fine distinction, or this one gezeirah shavah [verbal analogy] - this is "the word of the LORD he has despised." It is taught: Rabbi Meir would say, whoever learns Torah and does not teach it to others - this is "the word of the LORD he has despised." Rabbi Natan says: whoever does not pay attention to the Mishnah. Rabbi Nehorai says: whoever is able to occupy himself with Torah and does not. Rabbi Yishmael says: this refers to one who worships idolatry. From where do we derive that the school of Rabbi Yishmael meant this? From the fact that it teaches: this refers to one who demeans the statement the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses at Sinai, "I am the LORD," and so on, "you shall have no other gods," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:89: And concerning the matter of the heretic [apikoros], they say there: and "apikoros" - Rav and Rabbi Chanina both said, this refers to one who demeans Torah scholars. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and Rabbi Yonatan say: this refers to one who demeans his fellow in the presence of a Torah scholar. And they say there: some teach this concerning the latter clause, "one who shows favoritism in Torah not according to halachah" - Rav and Rabbi Chanina [say this refers to] one who demeans the face of a Torah scholar. Rabbi Yonatan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say this refers to one who demeans his fellow's face in the presence of a Torah scholar. Granted, according to the one who says [that "showing favoritism"] means demeaning Torah scholars themselves, then it follows that demeaning one's fellow in the presence of a Torah scholar is [the more severe category of] "apikoros." But according to the one who says that demeaning one's fellow in the presence of a Torah scholar is "showing favoritism," then who is [the more severe] "apikoros"? Rav Yosef said: one who says, what good have the Rabbis done for us - they read [Scripture] for their own benefit and study [Mishnah] for their own benefit. Abaye said to him: is that "apikoros"? That is [merely] "showing favoritism in the Torah," for it is written (Jeremiah 33:25), "were it not for My covenant day and night" (meaning that the Sages sustain the world). Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: you may also derive this from here (Genesis 18:26), "and I will forgive the whole place for their sakes." Rather, who is [truly called] "apikoros" [in this context]? Such as one who sits before his teacher, and a teaching comes up that was said elsewhere [by his teacher], and he says, "we say thus-and-such there," rather than "my master said thus-and-such there." Rava said: such as the members of the house of Binyamin the doctor, who would say, what good have the Rabbis done for us - they never permitted us the raven nor forbade us the dove [meaning, they never innovated any halachic ruling of practical value]. Rav Pappa said: such as one who says, "these rabbis" [in a demeaning tone]. Rav Pappa himself once slipped and said "these rabbis," and he sat in fasting [as penance]. Rav Nachman said: this refers to one who calls his teacher by his [first] name, as it is said (II Kings 8:5), "and Gechazi said, my lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha revived" [Gechazi referred to his master by name] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:90: Further, there is a twelfth distinction concerning the matter of honor, which is to honor one's Creator with praise and glorification, as it is said (Psalms 29:9), "and in His Temple all say, Glory!" - and we have elaborated on this matter in the Gate of Love, in the matter of joy, for that is its proper place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:91: And concerning the whole category of the distinction of honor that we have explained, it says in Tanna Devei Eliyahu, brought in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah 5:9), in these words: Elijah says, they gathered and went out to war, and fifty thousand men fell of them, and the Great Sanhedrin fell with them - who killed them? You must say, none but the men of Beit Shemesh killed them, because they looked upon the Ark; and therefore he warned the sons of Kehat (Numbers 4:20), "but they shall not go in to see," and so on. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: just as I did for the sons of Kehat, because they feared Me, I honored them and gave them honor and warned concerning them to save their souls from death - so too, whoever fears Me, I honor him and do not cut off his name from the world. From whom do you learn this? From the sons of Yonadav ben Rechav - because they performed My will, what is written of them (Jeremiah 35:19)? "Yonadav son of Rechav shall not lack a man to stand before Me forever." And if this is what I did for them, who were converts, how much more so for Israel, who are the children of My beloved, the children of My cherished one, when they perform My will - that they shall stand before Me forever, as it is said (Isaiah 48:18), "had you but hearkened to My commandments, then your peace would have been like a river," and so on; and it says (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to the LORD your God are all alive today" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:92: And we thought, to complete this Gate, to explain the verses of fear in the Torah, Prophets, and Writings that pertain to practical matters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:93: The first fear in the Torah, in the sin of Adam, is (Genesis 3:10), "and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself." And the matter is that Adam, before his sin, was clothed in garments of light; and after his sin, that supernal light was removed and stripped from him, and he became physical and clothed in garments of skin - and this is "and I was afraid" - he became afraid because he saw himself naked of the supernal light. And so too every person must have this distinction of fear, that he not cause, through his sin, the light of the Shechinah to depart from him - for through occupying himself with Torah and commandments, a person draws upon himself the light of the Shechinah, but if, Heaven forfend, he sins, it departs and he remains naked - and this is another distinction concerning the matter of fear of sin, beyond what I have explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:94: The second: to be careful of the fear of the Name all day, as it is said (Proverbs 23:17), "but be in the fear of the LORD all the day." And the pious Rabbeinu Yonah wrote in his Iggeret HaTeshuvah that it is a great pillar concerning the matter of Torah, that the fear of Heaven should not depart from before your eyes all day, as it is said, "but be in the fear of the LORD all the day"; and the plain sense of the verse, we must say, is this: "let your heart not envy sinners, but be in the fear of the LORD all the day" - meaning, do not envy sinners, but rather whom should you envy? Only the fear of the LORD, the virtue of the fear of the LORD - saying, why am I not one who fears the LORD all the day? And this is because sinners lack completeness, along the lines of "and I and my son Solomon will be deficient [chata'im]" - "but [be] in the fear of the LORD," like those who have the fear of the LORD all the day. It appears that one must be a fearer of the [divine] Name all day. And what reminds a person of fear is that he wear tefillin all day, if possible, or at least during the hours he is occupied with Torah, when he is free from worldly affairs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:95: And let him learn from the fact that the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded the king (Deuteronomy 17:19), "and it shall be with him, and he shall read from it all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the LORD," and so on - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained that a Torah scroll was always to be with him, and therefore he was warned about fear - and this is "that he may learn." In these words, in the Tosefta (Sanhedrin 4:4): when he goes out to war, it is with him; when he enters [his house], it is with him; when he sits in his house, it is beside him; when he enters the bathhouse, it waits for him at the door. And so David says (Psalms 16:8), "I have set the LORD always before me," and so on. Rabbi Yehudah says: the Torah scroll on his right and tefillin on his left. And it says further there: if so, why is it said (Deuteronomy 17:18), "and he shall write for himself a copy of this Torah"? This teaches that he writes two Torah scrolls for himself: one that goes in and out with him, and one that is placed for him within the house. The one that goes in and out with him shall not enter with him into the bathhouse nor into the privy - as it is said, "and it shall be with him, and he shall read from it," in a place fit to read in it. And these matters follow a kal vachomer: if the king of Israel, who is occupied only with the needs of the community, it is said of him, "and it shall be with him, and he shall read from it all the days of his life," how much more so for other people!
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:96: And along these lines (ibid. 34:9), "and Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands upon him," and so on; and so it says, "Joshua the son of Nun, a young man" (Exodus 33:11); and so it says (Joshua 1:8), "this book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night." And these matters follow a kal vachomer: if of Joshua son of Nun, who was occupied with the conquest of the Land and stood to divide it for Israel, it is said, "shall not depart," and so on, how much more so for other people! - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:97: Behold, the king needed to have a Torah scroll with him, and according to Rabbi Yehudah, also tefillin; and since it is not possible for [ordinary] people to have a Torah scroll [always with them], as we are not commanded in this, it is fitting to fulfill [the equivalent through] tefillin - and therefore the early Sages were careful to wear tefillin all day.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:98: And behold, certainly what reminds a person of fear is the occupation with Torah - for they said (Avot 2:5), "an ignoramus cannot fear sin" - and from this you see how great an obligation rests upon us to occupy ourselves with Torah, and from it fear is aroused, which is called "fear of the LORD," as it is said (Psalms 19:10), "the fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever." And the entire existence of the Torah scroll and tefillin is to remind one to occupy himself with Torah continually, as it is said (Exodus 13:9), "that the Torah of the LORD may be in your mouth" - and this is "this book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth," as explained in the discourse.
